sections.heading: C - New York Driver Manual Chapter Three: Owning a vehicle
sections.markdown:
## C - New York Driver Manual Chapter Three: Owning a vehicle

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Registration permits road use while the title proves ownership; registration needs age sixteen, titling any age, and new residents must register within thirty days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=24]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
Registering demands ownership or owner authorization, insurance, paid sales taxes, and odometer and damage statements on form MV-82 with six-point name and birth-date proof, per guide MV-82.1, yielding plates, a document and a sticker; non-dealer buys add a ten-day inspection extension on request, while dealer cars must carry an inspection from within thirty days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=24]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Registered dealers may register the car for the buyer with temporary paperwork and plates for a processing fee plus state fees. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=24]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
Dealer-new ownership is a manufacturer origin certificate plus MV-50 sale certificate, dealer-used is the prior MV-999 title with odometer and salvage statements plus MV-50, non-registering dealers must still hand over those papers with a signed MV-82, out-of-state-dealer used cars need signed-over title or transferable registration with bill and proofs, and private-used needs the signed-over MV-999 or a transferable registration for nineteen-seventy-two and older with signed odometer and damage acknowledgments. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=24]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A02
Before accepting any title, buyers check its face for lien holders showing unpaid vehicle loans, demand a lender release, or risk repossession by the lien holder [A02] [A01].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A02
Offices reject titles lacking completed odometer or damage statements or showing alterations, erasures or cancellations, even of a name or signature. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A02
Cars eight model years old or newer need both seller-completed and buyer-signed odometer and damage statements that may brand the new title Rebuilt Salvage; cars ten model years or newer need the odometer statement on the title back while damage disclosure drops off at nine model years and older, and buyers initial the odometer box and match it to the dash reading. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A02
Rebuilt Salvage or similar-worded vehicles must pass a stolen-parts examination before registration or titling, and out-of-state titled buys warrant a call-center check first. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A02
Registered dealers collect sales tax directly, while other sellers trigger form DTF-802 with buyer-completed price certification and a seller signature when the price trails market value or the car is a non-family gift, defaulting otherwise to market-value tax at registration. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A02
Insurers issue two identification cards whose names and VIN must match the application exactly, one presented at registration and one kept in the car. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A02
Most registrations to eighteen thousand pounds run two years on weight-based fees plus plate and title fees, used plates kill any refund, unused plates returned within sixty days refund fully minus processing, second-year fees refund when only the first year was used, plate turn-ins need receipt FS-6T, and transfer credit follows only the replacement vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A03
Sellers and traders strip plates and the windshield sticker first, or strangers parking tickets may bill the old owner. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=26]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A03
Renewals run every two years with mailed reminders forty-five to sixty days out, lost when addresses lapse, three-plus parking tickets stand unanswered, or credentials are suspended, plus two weeks of processing that the owner must anticipate without excuse. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=26]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A03
Expiries landing on weekends or state holidays stretch automatically to midnight of the next business day with insurance maintained throughout. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=26]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A03
Mail renewal files MV-82 with a separate note for alternate mailing, since addresses written on MV-82 join the record while MV-232 alone changes every record, plus a check to the Commissioner with MV-204A fee lookup and an insurance card when carriers changed, sent to the Utica processing center with two weeks of patience, longer overseas, and name changes demand an office visit with identity proofs. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=26]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A03
Online renewal fits unchanged addresses and carriers on passenger cars, small trucks and non-exclusive-off-road motorcycles, showing fees on screen for three-step credit-card renewal mailed within two weeks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=26]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A03
In-person renewal files MV-82 with the registrant's signature, and second parties including spouses must show original identification for themselves plus original or copy for the registrant. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=26]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A04
A registered vehicle must stay liability-insured whether driven or parked. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=27]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A04
Minimum coverage is fifty thousand for one death and one hundred thousand for two or more, twenty-five thousand for one injury and fifty thousand for two or more, and ten thousand for property, all per incident. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=27]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A04
Before coverage lapses, plates go back with an FS-6T receipt or daily civil penalties or registration suspension follow, ninety uninsured days without returned plates suspend the license too, DMV insurance letters demand answers, and motorcycles skip the plate turn-in. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=27]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A04
Everyone driving or lending a car in the state, resident or not, must prove acceptable insurance, and uninsured driving, lending or crashing revokes at least one year. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=27]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A04
In-state-sold vehicles need inspection within thirty days with a certificate before delivery, non-dealer buys need it within ten days of registration with a VS-1077 extension on request, and a mover's existing certificate survives to expiry or one year, whichever first. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=27]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A04
Retail inspection exemptions cover welfare-to-work transfers, chassis transfers, factory-direct delivery, out-of-state or country registration, scrap, and lease buyouts. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=27]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A04
Re-inspection falls due before the current certificate expires and on every registrant change, at yellow-and-black official stations, with heavy trucks, buses, tractors and trailers at heavy-vehicle stations and motorcycles at motorcycle stations. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=27]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A04
Signing a renewal certifies the inspection is current, owners track the annual date and book early for repair time, passers earn a windshield sticker while failures get a rejection notice demanding repair and retest. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=27]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A05
Failed high-enhanced or OBD II emissions inspections can waive after a genuine repair attempt costing at least four hundred fifty dollars; most gasoline cars take emissions with safety except motorcycles, and cars twenty-six-plus or under-two model years old plus historic registrations take safety only. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A05
Diesels running in the state face random roadside safety checks even when registered elsewhere, and ratings over eighty-five hundred pounds add a diesel emissions inspection. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A05
The DMV licenses dealers, stations and repair shops, so buyers verify credentials, complain to management first, then call weekdays eight-thirty to four-fifteen or write the Albany consumer box, with repair complaints due within ninety days or three thousand miles, whichever first. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=28]
